mainTopic: Seals on food left with a גוי, foods of a גוי that are forbidden, and the new משנה's list of foods that are permitted
overview: This amud deals with foods a Jew gets from a גוי or leaves with a גוי. It first finishes רב's list of which foods need two seals and which need only one. It explains why one seal is enough for bread, and it fixes רב's list so that it says 'a piece of fish without a sign' instead of milk. שמואל gives his own list, in which fish is simply counted as meat. A ברייתא then says that in סוריא certain foods may be bought only from an expert, but a guest may eat them at a host's home. This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that food a host sends from his home is permitted. The גמרא explains מלח סלקונדרית and the argument over whether its black or white kind is forbidden, and it explains what the משנה's closing words 'these are forbidden' leave out. A new משנה then lists foods of a גוי that are permitted to eat. The גמרא explains watched milk, honey, dripping grape clusters, unminced טרית, and brine with fish in it, and that last definition continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רב's list: which foods need two seals and which need one
steps.stepSummary: רב finishes his ruling. The foods listed before this point are forbidden with only one seal, while חילתית, מורייס, bread and cheese are permitted with one seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The items listed before this] are forbidden if they have only one seal. חילתית, fish stew, bread and cheese are permitted with one seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רב's list of foods left with a non-Jew. It sorts them into two groups: foods that need two seals, and foods that are fine with one seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seal protects food left with a non-Jew from being swapped or tampered with. Some foods are risky enough to need a double seal. Others need only a single seal. The rest of this section explains why certain items belong in the one-seal group.

keyTerms.meaning: A seal placed on food to show no one has tampered with it
A fish brine or fish stew

phrases.english: are forbidden with one seal.
Chiltit, fish stew, bread, cheese —
are permitted with one seal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement of רב that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some foods need two seals. חילתית, מורייס, bread and cheese need only one.

steps.title: Why might bread have needed two seals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what worry about bread could have made us think it needs more than one seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bread: what should we worry about with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to explain why bread is in the one-seal group. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To show why one seal is enough, the גמרא first asks what risk bread could carry. Once each possible risk is ruled out, the one-seal rule makes sense.

phrases.english: Bread, what should we worry about with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind one item in רב's one-seal list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What risk of swapping bread could have called for two seals

steps.title: Any bread swap would be noticed or is not worth the effort
steps.stepSummary: A swap of cold bread for warm bread, or barley bread for wheat bread, would be noticed. A swap of similar breads is not worth forging a seal for.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the worry is that he swaps cold bread for warm bread, that is easy to notice. Wheat for barley is also easy to notice. If the worry is swapping similar breads, then since there is a seal, he won't bother to forge one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through each possible swap and shows why one seal protects against all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of swap. A swap of different breads (old for fresh, barley for wheat) would be obvious, so no seal is even needed for that. A swap of identical breads gains the non-Jew nothing, so he will not go to the trouble of forging the seal.

keyTerms.meaning: Alike, the same as each other
He won't bother to forge (the seal)

steps.whatToRemember: One seal is enough when any swap would be obvious, or when forging a seal is not worth the small gain.

phrases.english: If it is because of swapping cold for warm —
that is clearly noticeable,
and wheat for barley is also clearly noticeable,
if they are alike —
since there is one seal,
he won't bother to forge it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about bread
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Swaps between different breads are noticeable, and swaps between identical breads are not worth forging a seal for, so one seal is enough.

steps.title: Why is cheese different from milk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: if cheese needs only one seal because no one will bother to forge a seal, the same should be true of milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב, why is cheese different? Because he won't bother to forge? With milk too he won't bother to forge!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's list. Milk is in the two-seal group but cheese is in the one-seal group, and the reason given for cheese seems to apply to milk as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning 'he won't bother to forge a seal' explained why cheese needs one seal. The גמרא says the same reasoning should apply to milk. That makes milk's place on the two-seal list look inconsistent.

phrases.english: And according to רב, why is cheese different?
Because he won't bother to forge?
With milk too he won't bother to forge!
phrases.notes: So milk should not need two seals either, yet רב listed it with the two-seal foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'won't bother to forge' reasoning to question another part of רב's list
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's placing milk in the two-seal group and cheese in the one-seal group
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason cheese needs only one seal applies equally to milk.

steps.title: רב כהנא: replace milk with fish that has no sign
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא changes the wording of רב's list. Milk is removed, and 'a piece of fish without a sign' is put in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Take out 'milk' and put in 'a piece of fish that has no sign.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of רב's statement. Milk was never on the two-seal list; a piece of fish without a sign was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once milk is removed, there is no conflict with cheese. A piece of fish without a sign could easily be swapped for non-kosher fish, so it needs two seals.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign (here, a sign showing the fish is kosher)

steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is not giving a new reason for milk. He is changing which item appears on רב's list.

phrases.english: רב כהנא said:
Take out 'milk',

phrases.aramaic: וְעַיֵּיל חֲתִיכַת דָּג שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ סִימָן.
phrases.english: and put in 'a piece of fish that has no sign.'
phrases.notes: Once the fish is cut up, you can no longer see the signs that would show it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about milk
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב listed milk as needing two seals
steps.terutzMaskana: רב listed a piece of fish without a sign, not milk

steps.title: Isn't fish the same as meat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that fish is just meat, which is already on the two-seal list.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as meat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא's correction. Meat is already on the two-seal list, so why would fish need to be listed separately?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fish counts as meat, adding it to the list repeats something already there. That makes the correction look unnecessary.

phrases.english: That is the same as meat!
phrases.notes: Meat was already listed among the foods that need two seals, before this section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's new wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fish is meat, and meat is already on the list.

steps.title: Two kinds of meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that animal meat and fish are two kinds of meat, and רב lists both.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that fish is not a repeat. רב mentions both kinds of meat, animal meat and fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought animal meat and fish follow different rules. Listing both shows that each needs two seals. This settles רב כהנא's correction.
steps.whatToRemember: Following רב כהנא, רב's two-seal list includes both animal meat and a piece of fish without a sign, but not milk.

phrases.english: Two kinds of meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection that fish repeats meat
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart two kinds within one category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fish is just meat, so listing it adds nothing
steps.terutzMaskana: Animal meat and fish are two kinds of meat, and both need two seals

steps.title: שמואל's own list of one-seal and two-seal foods
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a different list from רב's. Meat, wine and תכלת need two seals, while fish brine, חילתית and cheese need only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: B-Y-T are forbidden with one seal, M-Ch-G are allowed with one seal. Meat, wine and תכלת are forbidden with one seal; fish brine, חילתית and cheese are allowed with one seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings שמואל's version of the list. He uses letter codes and then spells out which foods they stand for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Foods where a swap would be worth the trouble of forging a seal need two seals. Foods where no one would bother to forge a seal are fine with one. Unlike רב's list as corrected by רב כהנא, שמואל's list does not mention a piece of fish. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: The sky-blue dye used for ציצית
A brine or sauce made from fish
A sharp-smelling plant resin used in food

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
B-Y-T is forbidden with one seal,
phrases.notes: These letters are a memory code. The very next line tells you what they stand for: בשר, יין, תכלת.

phrases.english: M-Ch-G is permitted with one seal.
Meat, wine, sky-blue dye
are forbidden with one seal;
fish brine, chiltit, cheese
are permitted with one seal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second אמורא's list after the back-and-forth over רב's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat, wine and תכלת need two seals. Fish brine, חילתית and cheese are fine with one seal.

steps.title: Why שמואל does not list fish separately
steps.stepSummary: שמואל does not mention an unmarked piece of fish because to him it is just meat. He does not split meat into two kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to שמואל, a piece of fish without a sign is the same as meat. We do not say there are two kinds of meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל's list leaves out the piece of fish that רב כהנא added to רב's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא said רב lists animal meat and fish as two kinds of meat. שמואל does not split them, so the word בשר already covers fish and he does not need to name it.

phrases.english: According to Shmuel,
a piece of fish that has no sign
is the same as meat,
we do not say two kinds of meat.
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of step 7, where רב was said to count animal meat and fish as two separate kinds.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁמוּאֵל, חֲתִיכַת דָּג שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ סִימָן הַיְינוּ בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why שמואל's list has no fish.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a missing item: it is already included under another word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think שמואל disagrees about fish because he does not mention it.
steps.terutzMaskana: For שמואל, fish is included in בשר, so it also needs two seals.
steps.whatToRemember: רב counts animal meat and fish as two kinds of meat. שמואל counts them as one, so the word בשר covers both.

steps.title: Buying sensitive foods in Syria only from an expert
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that in סוריא one may buy wine, fish brine, milk, מלח סלקונדרית, חילתית and cheese only from a trusted expert. A guest at a host's home may eat all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may not buy Y-M-Ch M-Ch-G in סוריא, not wine, fish brine, milk, מלח סלקונדרית, חילתית or cheese, except from an expert. And if one is a guest at a host's home, all of them are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about buying foods that are easy to mix with forbidden ingredients, when one is in סוריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When buying, one needs a seller known to be careful, an expert. But a guest eating at a host's table may trust the host, because a person keeps his own home kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert, a seller trusted to be careful

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not buy Y-M-Ch M-Ch-G in Syria,
phrases.notes: Another letter code. Each letter stands for one food in the next lines: יין, מורייס, חלב, מלח, חילתית, גבינה.

phrases.english: not wine and not fish brine
and not milk and not salkondarit salt
and not chiltit and not cheese,
except from the expert,

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלָּן אִם נִתְאָרַח אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: and all of them, if he was a guest at a host, are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the seal lists to a new ברייתא about buying these kinds of foods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In סוריא these six foods may be bought only from an expert, but a guest may eat them at a host's home.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The guest rule in the ברייתא supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who says that food a host sends to someone's house is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, for רבי יהושע בן לוי said: If a host sent him food to his house, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the end of the ברייתא backs up a ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא trusts a host for the food on his own table. רבי יהושע בן לוי takes the same trust one step further: even food the host sends to someone else's house is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁגֵּר לוֹ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לְבֵיתוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: If a host sent it to him at his house, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's last line as backing for an אמורא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling that food a host sends is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's rule that a guest may eat these foods at a host's home.

steps.title: Why a host's food can be trusted
steps.stepSummary: A host would not skip kosher food to eat forbidden food, and when he sends food he sends from what he himself eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? A host does not leave permitted food and eat forbidden food. And when he sends food to someone, he sends from what he eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts. First, a person keeps his own food kosher. Second, a gift comes from that same food. So even food that could not be bought from him is fine as a gift from his home.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
A host does not leave permitted food
and eat forbidden food,
and when he sends to him,
he sends him from what he eats.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לָא שָׁבֵיק הֶיתֵּירָא וְאָכֵל אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling cited in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A host eats only kosher food himself, and he sends gifts from his own food.
steps.whatToRemember: A host's own food is trusted, and so is food he sends from his home, because he sends from what he eats.

steps.title: What is מלח סלקונדרית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's phrase מלח סלקונדרית and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מלח סלקונדרית. What is מלח סלקונדרית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a term from the משנה and asks for its meaning. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a plain question about what a word means, not a challenge. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of salt that the משנה lists as forbidden

phrases.english: And salkondarit salt.
What is salkondarit salt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining a word from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term מלח סלקונדרית.

steps.title: The salt eaten by Roman bakers
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, says it is the salt that all the Roman bakers eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It is salt that all the Roman סלקונדרי eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying what kind of salt this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name comes from the people who used it, the סלקונדרי of Rome. The answer tells us what the salt is, not why it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: מֶלַח שֶׁכׇּל סַלְקוֹנְדְּרֵי רוֹמִי אוֹכְלִין אוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: Salt that all the bakers of Rome eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the salt eaten by all the Roman bakers.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about black and white salt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר says black מלח סלקונדרית is forbidden and white is permitted. רבי יהודה says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: מלח סלקונדרית: black is forbidden and white is permitted. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: white is forbidden and black is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about which color of this salt is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that one color is a problem and the other is not. They disagree about which color is which, and the text does not give their reasons.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: salkondarit salt,
black is forbidden,
white is permitted,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
white is forbidden, black is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the salt, brings a ברייתא about its laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids the black salt and permits the white. רבי יהודה forbids the white and permits the black.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. Each תנא forbids the color the other one permits.

steps.title: A third view: both colors are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן גמליאל, quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, says both black and white מלח סלקונדרית are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן גמליאל said in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: Both this one and that one are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a third opinion that forbids both kinds of the salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה each permit one color. This third view permits neither color, which is the strictest position.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: says in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel:
This and that are forbidden.
phrases.notes: He means both the black salt and the white salt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the מחלוקת in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both black and white מלח סלקונדרית are forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on מלח סלקונדרית. רבי מאיר forbids only the black, רבי יהודה forbids only the white, and רבי חנינא בן גמליאל forbids both.

steps.title: Why each opinion forbids black or white salt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that each opinion forbids the color of salt that has non-kosher fish intestines of that color mixed into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The one who forbids white salt holds that intestines of white non-kosher fish are mixed into it. The one who forbids black salt holds that intestines of black non-kosher fish are mixed into it. The one who forbids both holds that both kinds are mixed in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each opinion in the ברייתא about black and white מלח סלקונדרית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three opinions share the same basic concern: innards of non-kosher fish mixed into the salt. They disagree about which salt actually has those innards in it. The one who forbids white salt says white fish innards are mixed in, the one who forbids black salt says black fish innards are mixed in, and the third opinion says both are.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
According to the one who says white salt is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה from the ברייתא in step 15.

phrases.english: intestines of white non-kosher fish
are mixed into it.
According to the one who says black salt is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר from step 15.

phrases.english: intestines of black non-kosher fish
are mixed into it.
According to the one who says both are forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is the opinion from step 16.

phrases.english: both kinds are mixed into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the three opinions quoted in steps 15 and 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each opinion forbids salt because non-kosher fish innards of a matching color are mixed into it.

steps.title: An elder who smoothed the salt with pig fat
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, reports that an elder in רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's neighborhood used to smooth the surface of this salt with pig fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: There was an elder in our neighborhood who used to smooth its surface with pig fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another problem with מלח סלקונדרית: it was sometimes smoothed with pig fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a second reason to be careful with the salt, besides the fish innards. Here the problem is something forbidden smeared on the salt's surface, not something mixed into it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel:
There was a certain elder in our neighborhood
who would smooth its surface
with pig fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further reason that מלח סלקונדרית is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלח סלקונדרית was also forbidden because some people smoothed it with pig fat.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל

steps.title: What do the closing words 'these are forbidden' exclude
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's closing words 'הרי אלו אסורים' and asks what they come to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'These are forbidden.' What does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the end of the משנה and asks why it repeats that these items are forbidden. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already opened by saying these items are forbidden to eat. Saying 'these are forbidden' again at the end seems unnecessary. So the גמרא assumes the extra words must be teaching something by leaving something else out.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to exclude?

phrases.english: 'These are forbidden.'
What does this come to exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the salt discussion and turns to the משנה's closing phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra closing words 'הרי אלו אסורים' come to exclude.

steps.title: The answer according to חזקיה and according to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: For חזקיה, the words exclude cases where we know wine was added. For רבי יוחנן, they exclude מורייס and the cheese of בית אונייקי, and this unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to חזקיה, it excludes cases where it is known that wine was added. According to רבי יוחנן, it excludes מורייס and the cheese of בית אונייקי. And the unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two versions, one following each side of the earlier argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'these are forbidden' mean forbidden only to eat, not forbidden to benefit from. So they leave out cases that are worse, where even benefit is forbidden. The two אמוראים disagree about which cases those are. For רבי יוחנן, this means the משנה matches רבי מאיר, who forbids benefit from those items.

keyTerms.meaning: Where it is known (that wine of a גוי was added)
Cheese from the place called בית אונייקי
An unnamed statement in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: 'הרי אלו אסורים' means forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit. It excludes the stricter cases: for חזקיה, where wine was surely added; for רבי יוחנן, מורייס and the cheese of בית אונייקי, following רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: According to Ḥizkiyya, it excludes the case where it is known,
phrases.notes: Known that wine of a גוי was put in. Then even benefit is forbidden.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, it excludes fish brine
and the cheese of Beit Unyaki,
and the unnamed משנה follows Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר, in the earlier משנה on 29b, forbids even benefit from these.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For חזקיה: it excludes known cases of added wine. For רבי יוחנן: it excludes מורייס and the cheese of בית אונייקי, so the משנה follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: New משנה: foods of a גוי that are permitted to eat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists foods from a גוי that a Jew may eat: watched milk, honey, dripping grape clusters, certain pickles, unminced טרית fish, brine with fish in it, the חילתית leaf, and rolled olive cakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are permitted to eat: milk that a גוי milked while a Jew watched him; honey; grape clusters, which even though they drip are not subject to הכשר משקה; pickled foods that are not usually made with wine and vinegar; טרית fish that is not minced; brine that has fish in it; the leaf of the חילתית plant; and rolled olive cakes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists foods from a גוי that are permitted to eat, the opposite of the list of forbidden foods we just finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is permitted because the reason for concern is missing. A Jew watched the milking. Pickles that are not normally made with wine are not suspected of having wine. Whole fish and brine with fish in it can be checked as kosher. The line about grapes adds a side rule: their dripping juice does not make them ready to become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the start of a new משנה)
Liquid that makes food able to become טמא
A plant whose resin was used as a spice

steps.confusionAlert: The words about הכשר משקה are not about כשרות. They are a side rule about טומאה: the juice dripping from the grapes does not make them able to become טמא.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are permitted to eat:
milk that a gentile milked while a Jew watched him,
and honey, and grape clusters,
which, even though they are dripping,
are not made ready for טומאה by that liquid,
and pickled foods that are not usually made
by putting wine and vinegar into them,
and טרית fish that is not minced,
and brine that has a fish in it,
and the leaf of the חילתית plant,
and rolled olive cakes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה that balances the previous list of forbidden foods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Certain foods of a גוי are permitted to eat when the usual reason for concern is not present.

steps.title: רבי יוסי on overripe olives and locusts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that overripe olives are forbidden. Locusts from a seller's basket are forbidden, but locusts from a storeroom are permitted. The same distinction applies to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Overripe olives are forbidden. Locusts that come from a seller's basket are forbidden, but those from the storeroom are permitted. The same applies to תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. רבי יוסי adds his own rulings about a few more foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה listed foods from a גוי that are permitted (step 21). רבי יוסי now names items he considers forbidden, and he separates locusts by where they come from. He also says the same rule works for תרומה, which the גמרא will explain later.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Overripe olives are forbidden;
locusts that come from the seller's basket are forbidden;
those from the storeroom are permitted;
and the same is true for תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's list from step 21 with רבי יוסי's added rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Overripe olives and locusts from a seller's basket are forbidden. Locusts from a storeroom are permitted, and the same distinction applies to תרומה.

steps.title: The משנה matches a ברייתא about watching a גוי milk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by pointing out that the משנה's ruling on watched milk is the same as a ברייתא. That ברייתא lets a Jew sit beside a גוי's flock while the גוי milks.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה teaches what the Rabbis taught in a ברייתא. A Jew may sit beside a גוי's flock while the גוי milks and brings him the milk, and he does not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by linking the משנה's 'milk that a Jew watched' to a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a Jew who is just sitting near the flock is watching enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase תנינא tells us the ברייתא adds no new law, because the משנה already teaches it. The surprising detail is that the Jew is sitting, not standing over the גוי. This sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: Gemara: We have learned in our משנה what the Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: He's pointing back to 'milk that a Jew watched' from the משנה's list in step 21.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹשֵׁב יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּצַד עֶדְרוֹ שֶׁל גּוֹי,
phrases.english: A Jew may sit beside a גוי's flock,
and the גוי milks and brings the milk to him,
and he need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא and connects the משנה's watched-milk rule to a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew sitting next to a גוי's flock while the גוי milks is enough supervision, and the milk is permitted.

steps.title: What case does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is talking about. If there are no non-kosher animals in the flock, the ruling is obvious. If there are, why is a sitting Jew enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If there is no non-kosher animal in his flock, it's obvious. And if there is a non-kosher animal in his flock, why is it permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with two options, and neither one seems to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no non-kosher animal in the flock, there is nothing to worry about, so why teach it? With a non-kosher animal there, the גוי could mix in non-kosher milk while the Jew isn't looking. Either way, the ברייתא seems hard to understand.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If there is no non-kosher animal in his flock,
it's obvious that the milk is fine;
and if there is a non-kosher animal in his flock,
why is it permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case of the ברייתא quoted in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does the ברייתא mean, given that both options seem to fail?
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's permission for a sitting Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a non-kosher animal the ruling is too obvious to teach. With one, a sitting Jew who can't see should not be enough.

steps.title: The גוי is afraid the Jew might stand and see
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really is talking about a flock with a non-kosher animal. The Jew can't see while sitting, but he could see if he stood up. That is enough to scare the גוי away from mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, there is a non-kosher animal. When the Jew stands he can see, but when he sits he can't. You might have thought that since he sits and can't see, we should worry the גוי will bring non-kosher milk and mix it in. So the ברייתא teaches that since the Jew could see by standing, the גוי is afraid and doesn't mix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a flock with a non-kosher animal. The sitting Jew's ability to stand up and look is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that real supervision doesn't need constant watching. It is enough that the גוי fears being caught. That is why the ruling is not obvious and is worth teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually (the גמרא keeps one side of the question)

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew who could see the milking just by standing up counts as watching. The גוי's fear of being caught keeps him from mixing in non-kosher milk.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical standard for supervising milk from a גוי: the Jew doesn't have to watch every moment.

phrases.english: Actually, it is a case where there is a non-kosher animal,
and when the Jew stands he can see the גוי,
but when he sits he cannot see him;
you might have said:
since he is sitting and cannot see him,
let us worry that perhaps the גוי will bring non-kosher milk and mix it in;
so it teaches us:
since when the Jew stands he can see him,
the גוי is afraid and does not mix anything into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by choosing the second option and explaining why it still works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The flock has a non-kosher animal. A sitting Jew is enough because he could stand and see, so the גוי is afraid to mix.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the sitting Jew can't see, we should worry about mixing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chance that the Jew stands up and sees is enough to stop the גוי from mixing.

steps.title: Why would we worry about honey at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'and the honey' from the משנה and asks what concern there could even be about a גוי's honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the honey.' Honey, what should we worry about with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list, honey, and asks why it would need to be mentioned as permitted. This sets up the next step, which goes through the possible concerns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Listing honey as permitted suggests someone might have thought it was forbidden. The גמרא wants to know what that worry could be.

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'And the honey.'
Honey, what should we worry about with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from milk to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What concern about a גוי's honey would make it worth saying it is permitted?

steps.title: Three possible worries about honey all fail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules out three concerns. Mixing in wine would spoil the honey. בישולי גוים doesn't apply because honey is eaten raw. גיעולי גוים doesn't apply because absorbed taste would be נותן טעם לפגם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the worry is mixing, the honey would spoil. If it's בישולי גוים, honey is eaten raw as it is. If it's גיעולי גוים, any absorbed taste spoils the honey's flavor, so it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through three possible reasons honey might be forbidden and rejects each one. So honey from a גוי is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each worry fails for its own reason. A גוי wouldn't mix wine into honey because that ruins it. Honey isn't cooked, so בישולי גוים doesn't apply. Taste absorbed from a גוי's pots would only make the honey worse, and a taste that spoils the food does not forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden taste absorbed from a גוי's vessels
A taste that spoils the food rather than improving it

steps.whatToRemember: Honey from a גוי is permitted because none of the three usual concerns applies: mixing, cooking, or absorbed taste.

phrases.english: If it is because of mixing,
phrases.notes: The worry is that the גוי mixed in something forbidden, like wine.

phrases.english: the honey would spoil, so he wouldn't do it;
if it is because of food cooked by a גוי,
honey is eaten as it is, raw;
if it is because of taste absorbed from a גוי's vessels,
that taste would spoil the honey, so it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by rejecting every possible concern about honey.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: None of the concerns applies. Mixing would spoil the honey, honey is eaten raw, and absorbed taste would be נותן טעם לפגם, so honey is permitted.

steps.title: Dripping grape clusters contradicted by the winepress case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that dripping grape clusters are not made ready for טומאה by their juice. It contradicts this with a ברייתא where הלל agreed with שמאי that grapes picked for the press are made ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: grape clusters, even though they drip juice, do not become ready for טומאה because of that liquid. But a ברייתא says otherwise. When someone picks grapes for the winepress, שמאי says they become ready for טומאה, הלל says they do not, and in the end הלל agreed with שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה and immediately raises a contradiction from another source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only get טומאה after it has been wet by a liquid; this is called הכשר. The משנה says juice dripping from grape clusters does not do this. But in the winepress case, juice coming out of grapes does do it, since even הלל ended up agreeing. So which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: Grape clusters (or berries) that drip juice
Making food ready to receive טומאה by wetting it with a liquid
'And they pointed out a contradiction': a source that seems to say the opposite
One who picks grapes to take them to the winepress

steps.confusionAlert: הכשר here has nothing to do with being kosher to eat. It is about whether food has become able to receive טומאה (ritual impurity).

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] And grape clusters, even though they are dripping,
they are not made ready for impurity by the liquid.
And they contradicted it: one who picks grapes for the winepress —
שמאי says: they have become ready for impurity,
הלל says: they have not become ready,
and הלל conceded to שמאי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from honey to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that dripping grape clusters are not made ready for טומאה by their juice.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The winepress case, as finally agreed by both שמאי and הלל, shows that juice seeping from grapes does make them ready for טומאה.

steps.title: It depends on whether he wants the juice
steps.stepSummary: The winepress picker wants the juice as a drink, so it makes the grapes ready. In the משנה's case nobody wants the juice, so it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he wants the juice as a drink. Here, he does not want it as a drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by pointing out a difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A liquid only makes food ready for טומאה if the owner is interested in that liquid. Someone picking for the press is making wine, so he wants the juice. Grape clusters that just drip, with no plan to collect the juice, are not affected.
steps.whatToRemember: For הכשר, what matters is not just whether liquid touched the food, but whether the owner wanted that liquid.

phrases.english: There, he wants it as a liquid,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the winepress case; 'here' means the grape clusters in our משנה.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא לָא קָא בָעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַשְׁקֶה.
phrases.english: here, he does not want it as a liquid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases based on intention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Juice from grapes always makes them ready for טומאה, as in the winepress case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Juice only makes them ready when the owner wants it as a drink. The winepress picker does; the owner of dripping clusters does not.

steps.title: Defining טרית that is not minced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'טרית that is not minced' from the משנה. A ברייתא defines it as any fish whose head and spine can still be recognized.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and טרית that is not minced. The Rabbis taught: what is טרית that is not minced? Any fish whose head and spine can be recognized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another item from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains exactly what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows טרית fish from a גוי as long as it is not minced. The ברייתא gives the test: if you can still recognize the head and spine, it counts as not minced.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of fish, often salted or pickled

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] And טרית that is not minced:

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, אֵיזוֹ הִיא טָרִית שֶׁאֵינָהּ טְרוּפָה?
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: what is טרית that is not minced?
Any whose head and spine are recognizable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, אֵיזוֹ הִיא טָרִית שֶׁאֵינָהּ טְרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from grape clusters to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טרית counts as 'not minced' when its head and spine can still be recognized.

steps.title: Defining brine that has fish in it
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues and defines brine that has fish in it as brine with one or two כילבית fish in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is brine that has fish in it? Any brine that has one כילבית or two כילביות in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to define the next item in the משנה, brine with fish in it. The sentence continues in the next lines of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also allowed brine that has fish in it. The ברייתא explains that this means brine with even one or two כילבית fish in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Brine, the salty liquid from pickled fish
A type of small fish (plural: כִּילְבִּיּוֹת)

phrases.english: And what is brine that has fish in it?

phrases.aramaic: כָּל שֶׁכִּילְבִּית אַחַת אוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּילְבִּיּוֹת
phrases.english: Any in which one כילבית or two כילביות

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from טרית to brine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brine counts as 'having fish in it' when one or two כילבית fish are in it.
